entries.name: The Church of the East — Three Patriarchates
entries.statusDescription: Tiered Viable, secondary (Tier 2): the sources are mostly outside witnesses. Its window runs from 1650 to 1815, the years between the two entries on either side of it. Not yet reviewed.
entries.sourcing:
The evidence is thin. Most texts come from outside the mountain church.

Badger was an English churchman who disliked Rome's work. Wigram led a church mission to the Assyrians. Labourt wrote for a Catholic reference work.

Malech was an Assyrian Protestant from Urmia. He gives the mountain side in a few lines. Labourt says few documents survive for these years.
entries.relationsSummary: This entry carries the Church of the East from 1650 to 1815. It follows the Schism of 1552 and leads on to the Chaldean Consolidation. Popes and missionaries shaped these years, and the entry on the Catholic Church of the Ancien Régime tells their side.
entries.why: The Church of the East had two patriarchs in 1650, one in the mountains and one on the plain. In 1681 the pope named a third, at Diyarbakır. In 1778 the patriarch of the plain turned to Rome, and his nephew wrote down the date: 30 April.
entries.longDescription:
The Church of the East began these years with two rival patriarchs. One lived in the mountains of Hakkari, at the village of Qudshanis. The other lived on the plain, at Alqosh and Mosul.

Each patriarch of the plain held an order from the Sultan, called a firman. It confirmed his power over his people in the empire. The mountain patriarchs had no such order. Badger writes that the Kurdish emirs tolerated and protected them.

Rome then added a third line. In 1672 Joseph, the church's archbishop at Diyarbakır, broke with the patriarch Elias. Labourt says he followed the advice of Capuchin missionaries. In 1681 Pope Innocent XI gave him the pallium and the title of patriarch. Wigram dates the new line to 1680.

Five men named Joseph held this see in turn. Badger says neither the old bishops nor the Ottoman government recognized the line at first. It did not reach beyond Diyarbakır.

In 1778 the patriarch of the plain turned to Rome. Elia died of plague at Alqosh on 29 April. His nephew Hormizd wrote the next part himself: “So on the 30th of April I embraced all that the holy Church believes.” After this, Wigram says, the Joseph line at Diyarbakır was allowed to lapse.
entries.teaser: Diyarbakır, Mosul and the Hakkari mountains, 1650 to 1815. An ancient church with three patriarchs at once. In 1778 the patriarch of the plain turned to Rome.
voices: Yohannan Hormizd — nephew of the patriarch Elia, who tells in his own account how he turned to Rome on 30 April 1778
Joseph — archbishop of Diyarbakır, who broke with the patriarch Elias in 1672 and became the first of the Catholic patriarchs named Joseph
Elia — patriarch of the East at Alqosh and Mosul, who died of plague on 29 April 1778
Denkha Shimon — patriarch of the mountain line, whose seat moved to Qudshanis in Ottoman territory
entries.legacy: By 1815 the church stood divided. The line of the plain had joined Rome. The line of the mountains stayed outside Rome's obedience. Its later story is told in the entry on the Church of the East and the Chaldean Consolidation.
